claim: Far-field (distant) examples raise novelty and widen quality spread but cost about one concept of output; the benefit shows only when far examples are also uncommon. Mean quality does not change.
agent_test: Give the agent far vs near vs no source prompts at equal tokens on a design task; score novelty (blind judge), quantity, quality SD.

claim: Patent-stimulus distance effects conflict across studies: Song 2017 found far-only and home+far gave higher quality while near-containing sets gave higher novelty (opposite of Chan 2011 on novelty); Chan, Dow & Schunn 2015 snippet says support for far sources is mixed with tiny cells.
agent_test: Run distance as a swept factor (near, mid, far) rather than binary; report novelty and quality separately, 3+ seeds.
note: Liu 2026 (d09): originality rises monotonically with semantic distance for humans and LLMs, no inverted U seen; strong LLMs gain only on the farthest pairs. Still no direct near-mid-far sweep of quality.

claim: Surface-similar inspirations are no better than random ones; sources matched on purpose but distant in mechanism give the most good ideas (46% vs 30% surface vs 37% random on nine shared seeds, human crowd, N=38).
agent_test: Retrieve sources by function/purpose abstraction versus keyword similarity; compare accepted-idea rate at equal tokens.

claim: Structured representations (purpose/mechanism vectors, functional aspects, entity-relation graphs) find analogous items better than surface text similarity (TF-IDF, LSA, LDA).
agent_test: Index memory entries by abstract role description as well as text; compare recall of useful analogues at fixed retrieval budget.

claim: In natural product design, analogies are frequent (11.3 per hour) and 45% are between-domain; in molecular-biology labs distant analogies are rare (Dunbar, second-hand). Distance depends on setting and on function (problem identification mostly near, explanation mostly far).
agent_test: Log analogy distance by function in agent traces; check whether far sources appear mainly in explain steps.

claim: Having a concrete prototype/exemplar at hand reduces analogy use; analogies appear mostly for unsupported ideas.
agent_test: Compare analogy generation when a draft solution is present vs absent in context.

claim: A far analogy can satisfy several constraints and still fail on one hidden constraint; LLMs also produce infeasible creative solutions (GPT-4 37.5% infeasible on MacGyver).
agent_test: After any analogical proposal, force an explicit constraint audit; count infeasible proposals with and without audit.

claim: LLMs match or beat humans on near, familiar analogy formats (Digit Matrices OR 1.88, letter strings OR 1.76, verbal analogies, near stories) but not on far-domain or counterfactual formats (far stories n.s., ARN far 39.6% vs human 94.1%, permuted alphabets 0.35-0.49 vs human 0.753, Stevenson symbol domain GPT-4o .48 vs adults .89, KidsARC).
agent_test: Test the agent on far-transfer analogy items with relation-preserving but surface-different wording; log gap to near condition.

claim: Whether GPT-class models have emergent analogical reasoning on letter strings is contested: failures on permuted alphabets (Lewis & Mitchell) versus the reply that GPT-4 with code execution matches humans (P=0.496).
agent_test: Evaluate the agent on counterfactual letter-string items with tool use on and off.

claim: Distractors that resemble the query on the surface hurt models more than humans (ARN: far analogy with near distractor 29.1% for GPT-4); in the radiation-problem demo, GPT-3 lost the solution when distractor stories were added until hinted.
agent_test: Insert surface-similar but relationally wrong sources into context; measure drop and the effect of a 'check relations first' step.

claim: An explicit abstraction step helps far analogy: chain-of-thought demos that first state each story's high-level message gave up to +30 points on far ARN analogies (while lowering near accuracy), and a self-written knowledge step before exemplars added 2 points on Codeforces.
agent_test: Add 'state the abstract relation first' before mapping; compare far vs near accuracy at equal tokens (watch the near-analogy cost).
note: Step-Back (d13) helps single-problem reasoning (GPT-4 Physics 84.5 vs CoT 82.9) but adds 11.9% new errors; Gick and Holyoak Exp 2-3 found a stated principle or diagram gave no gain (32% vs 29% before hint), while a self-induced schema from two analogs did (45% vs 21%). Not yet tested on far analogy at equal tokens.

claim: Analogical prompting (model recalls its own related problems) gives small gains over 0-shot CoT: GSM8K GPT-3.5 77.8 vs 75.8, MATH 37.3 vs 33.9, text-davinci-003 GSM8K 61.0 vs 50.3. Row labels in some extracts were shifted; corrected against the paper's Table 1.
agent_test: Self-generated exemplars vs none at equal tokens on in-house tasks.

claim: The relevance of self-generated exemplars is doubtful: Qin et al. found irrelevant or random self-generated examples did as well or better (GSM8K+MATH average relevant 52.4 vs no instruction 55.8 vs random biology 54.9), and example correctness mattered more.
agent_test: Run relevant vs random-exemplar controls whenever an analogy step is credited with a gain.

claim: Benefit of self-generated exemplars grows with model strength; retrieved real exemplars help weaker models more.
agent_test: Check at our model sizes; use retrieval of verified exemplars for small models.

claim: LLMs can produce meaningful analogies: the share judged meaningful rose with size to 70.05% at 175B vs 66.67% human reference; supplying a source hurt the largest model (70.05 to 53.79). A design study found one-shot examples gave 80% potentially useful vs 40% zero-shot, with about a quarter of analogies flagged potentially harmful.
agent_test: Generate analogies with a one-shot example; have a separate check step label harmful or misleading ones.

claim: Retrieving or rewriting against prior work raises novelty in about half of cases (SciMON 47-58%); LLM research ideas are rated more novel than expert ideas (5.64 vs 4.84) but collapse into duplicates (only about 5% unique of 4000 seeds).
agent_test: Measure novelty and duplicate rate of agent outputs across seeds when analogy retrieval is on.
note: Shen 2026 (d11) shows baseline duplicate collapse and that an analogy step restores diversity (Vendi +90-173%).

claim: Unprompted spontaneous transfer is rare in humans. Gick and Holyoak (as summarised in their 1983 paper, opened): about 10% of controls solve the radiation problem, about 30% after memorising the analogous story with no hint, about 75-80% in total once hinted. Checked in 1983 Exp 1-4 (pendulum problem 71% vs 20% before hint; 98% vs 30% total).
agent_test: Trigger analogy use explicitly: compare agent with an always-on 'what is this like?' step vs on-demand.
note: Numbers now read from the 1983 paper. The 1980 paper itself was not opened.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Strong LLMs do not gain originality from a random source prompt overall; the gain appears only when source-target distance is large (o3 and Claude-Sonnet-4: effect 0.02 over all pairs, 0.12 on the farthest 50%, 0.24 on the farthest 10%). Humans gain at nearly any distance.
agent_test: Sweep source distance for the agent and drop sources below a distance floor; log originality by distance bin.

claim: Humans' most original cross-domain ideas lose usefulness and feasibility (top 10%: utility lower by 0.81, p<.001); LLM ideas keep usefulness, and LLMs transfer structure and function rather than surface features.
agent_test: Score novelty and utility separately; check that the agent transfers a relation, not a surface feature.

claim: An explicit analogy pipeline (extract relational structure, find cross-domain analogues, map back) beats a plain cross-domain prompt at equal call count on diversity (Vendi +90-173%) and binary novelty (e.g. Claude 21.6 -> 50.4%), but humans rate its solutions reasonable less often (67% vs 86%).
agent_test: Use an analogy step for diversification, then add a feasibility audit; measure reasonable-rate at equal tokens.

claim: Reasoning models (o3-mini, DeepSeek R1) still collapse on out-of-distribution symbolic analogy under noise (86.6 -> 17.0 and 80.6 -> about 23); extra reasoning effort raised tokens up to 53596 for 31.0% accuracy. Longer thinking does not fix it.
agent_test: Do not rely on longer thinking for analogy robustness; report equal-token controls. Verbal far-analogy tests on 2025-2026 models are still missing.

claim: Two source cases plus an induced shared schema transfer better than one case (45% vs 21% before hint, 80% vs 53% total, Gick and Holyoak 1983 Exp 4); quality of the written schema tracks transfer (good schema 91% before hint).
agent_test: When retrieving analogues, supply two and ask the agent to state what they share before applying.

claim: Gap check, no evidence found: no study of reasoning-model reruns of relevant-vs-random exemplars (Qin), no equal-token test of analogy vs extra sampling, no test of analogical retrieval from an agent's own task memory, and no exact Dunbar in vivo counts (secondary source only: 98% local or regional).
agent_test: Run these as our own experiments.
